title: Phantom traffic insulation and cost governor for safe mirrored workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We regularly run mirrored/shadow traffic to validate candidate model revisions without impacting production outputs. Current mirror tooling replicates requests into a shadow tier but lacks per-tenant budget isolation, adaptive sampling decay, and a hard cost governor. As a result we see occasional invoice spikes from large tenants and unreliable rollback signals when shadow-induced errors correlate with upstream load spikes.

Goal: Implement a "phantom traffic insulation" layer and a cost-governor service that together ensure mirrored traffic is safely duplicated with: (1) per-tenant mirrored budget tokens, (2) adaptive sampling that decays sampling rate under budget pressure and SLO stress, (3) request tagging and strict side-effect suppression, and (4) a soft-to-hard circuit breaker with automatic tenant quarantine and rollback triggers for canary rollouts.

Proposed design:
- Mirroring proxy extension: introduce a lightweight proxy stage that applies per-request policies before duplication. The proxy consults a Budget API and Sampling Policy. If budget exhausted, the request is skipped or sampled at minimal rate.
- Budget API: per-tenant counters (monthly window + burst tokens) that charge mirrored token consumption separately from production billing. Budgets configurable by tenant via Dedicated/Private UI and defaulted for hosted.
- Adaptive sampling algorithm: starts from configured base rate (e.g., 10%) and reduces sampling with an exponential decay when mirrored CPU/latency cost or error rates grow beyond thresholds. Decay factors are shaped by recent KV cache hit ratio and inferred latency tails.
- Isolation guarantees: mirrored requests must never call side-effecting downstreams. Enforce via request header enforcement and a runtime validator that rejects duplication for endpoints that are not idempotent. Add a runtime whitelist for allowed endpoints.
- Cost governor & circuit breaker: a multistage controller that exposes soft limits (rate reduction + notification), followed by hard limits (tenant quarantine and kill-switch). Hard actions trigger a canary rollback policy if the candidate model is actively in a rollout.
- Observability: add per-tenant mirrored cost dashboards, SLO correlation charts, and a mirrored-trace tag in Console to surface mirror-origin traces.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype Budget API (2w): in-memory budgets + eviction, API + admin endpoints.
2) Extend mirror proxy (3w): policy enforcement hook + sampling plugin + logging.
3) Adaptive sampler and decay controller (2w): simulation harness and live toggle.
4) Circuit breaker & rollback integration (2w): define thresholds, integrate with rollout engine (canary/A-B), and add automated rollback webhook.
5) Ops and runbook (1w): incident playbook, cost alerts, and tenant notification templates.

Metrics and success criteria:
- Mirrored spend per tenant capped to configured budget 95% of time.
- Automatic rollback executed within 5 minutes of crossing hard error threshold during a canary.
- Latency tail increase due to shadow processing < 2% for P95 production latency.
- Reduced billing spikes: top-10 mirrored spend anomalies eliminated over 30 days.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Where to persist budgets for Private customers (local KVS vs control plane). Recommend pluggable storage with default control-plane-backed mode.
- Sampling fairness vs statistical power: lower sampling reduces signal for regression detection. Need to choose conservative decay schedule and provide a manual override.
- Handling long-running streaming requests: duplication of streams requires special gating to avoid double charges; propose not duplicating streaming sessions by default and adding an explicit opt-in.

Links / artifacts:
- Design sketch (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/PHANTOM-Traffic-Insulation
- Simulator harness (repo): https://github.com/redwood-inference/mirror-sim/pulls/78
- Initial PR for proxy hooks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1029

Next tasks (assignee):
- Marco: spin up Budget API prototype and add admin endpoints.
- Priya Nair: draft UI settings for tenant mirrored budgets in Console.
- Liam O'Connor: implement sampling plugin hooks in proxy and wire metrics.

Risks:
- Incorrect sampling decay may mask regressions. Mitigation: ship as opt-in for canaries and require escalation to enable for production test harnesses.
- Edge-case side-effects on downstreams. Mitigation: conservative endpoint whitelist and runtime guardrails.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit/integration tests for Budget API and proxy sampling.
- Canary rollout test with synthetic traffic that triggers automated rollback on injected error budget exceed.
- Dashboard with per-tenant mirrored cost and sampling rate visible in Console.
